annotation_provenance: Agent-authored engineering references frozen before inference, not expert philosophical annotations.

cases.source: If this punishment is justified, it is proportionate. This punishment is justified. So it is proportionate.
Consent is genuine only if it is informed. This consent is not informed. Therefore this consent is not genuine.
If this decision is autonomous, it is deliberate. This decision is deliberate. Hence it is autonomous.
If the promise is binding, breaking it is wrong. The promise is not binding. Thus breaking it is not wrong.
Either this theory is incomplete or this objection fails, or both. This theory is not incomplete. Therefore this objection fails.
Either the testimony is sincere or it is accurate, or both. The testimony is sincere. So it is not accurate.
This act is voluntary and informed. Therefore this act is informed.
This preference is coherent. This preference is stable. Thus this preference is coherent and stable.
It is not the case that the policy is fair and effective. The policy is fair. Therefore the policy is not effective.
The explanation is neither complete nor circular. Therefore it is not circular.
The verdict is correct if and only if the argument is sound. The argument is sound. Consequently the verdict is correct.
The proposal is acceptable unless it is coercive, where unless means that if it is not coercive then it is acceptable. The proposal is not coercive. So the proposal is acceptable.
Being consistent is necessary for this view to be defensible. This view is consistent. Therefore this view is defensible.
Being impartial is sufficient for this procedure to be fair. This procedure is impartial. Therefore this procedure is fair.
This choice is rational. This choice is not rational. Therefore this choice is free.
The intuition is reliable. Hence the intuition is reliable.
This action maximizes welfare. Therefore this action is morally right.
cases.note: Do not add a utilitarian bridge to the explicit premises. Any proposed bridge must stay implicit.

cases.source: If the evidence is misleading, this belief is unjustified. The evidence is misleading. Thus this belief is unjustified. If this belief is unjustified, it is not knowledge. Therefore this belief is not knowledge.
An objector claims that the contract is fair. I reject that claim: if the contract is coerced, it is not fair. The contract is coerced. Therefore the contract is not fair.
cases.note: Reporting the objector is not endorsement; the conditional is the author's premise.

cases.source: This seminar concerns moral testimony. If the witness is dishonest, this report is unreliable. The witness is dishonest. Hence this report is unreliable.
The argument is sound if the evidence is decisive. The evidence is decisive. Therefore the argument is sound.
It is false that this inference is not valid. Therefore this inference is valid.
Exactly one of these claims holds: the action is obligatory, or the action is forbidden. The action is obligatory. Therefore the action is not forbidden.
cases.note: Treat obligation and prohibition as atoms; their exclusivity is an asserted premise, not an imported deontic axiom.

cases.source: If the reason is conclusive, the doubt is defeated. If the doubt is defeated, the inquiry is settled. Therefore if the reason is conclusive, the inquiry is settled.
Every person who consents is informed. Mira is a person who consents. Therefore Mira is informed.
Every perfect judge is impartial. Therefore at least one perfect judge is impartial.
No coercive act is voluntary. Some act is coercive. Hence some act is not voluntary.
Not every belief is justified. Therefore some belief is not justified.
Every person trusts some person. Therefore some person is trusted by every person.
claims: (forall x (implies (Person x) (exists y (and (Person y) (Trusts x y)))))
(exists y (and (Person y) (forall x (implies (Person x) (Trusts x y)))))

cases.source: Lina is identical to the witness. The witness is honest. Therefore Lina is honest.
Every virtue is admirable. Everything admirable is valuable. Therefore every virtue is valuable.
Some person respects every person. Therefore every person is respected by some person.
claims: (exists x (and (Person x) (forall y (implies (Person y) (Respects x y)))))
(forall y (implies (Person y) (exists x (and (Person x) (Respects x y)))))

cases.source: Necessarily, every truth is true. Therefore every truth is true.
cases.reason: Modal necessity and its elimination need modal semantics.

cases.source: If the agent had chosen otherwise, the outcome would have changed. The outcome did not change. Therefore the agent did not choose otherwise.
cases.reason: Counterfactual dependence is not material implication.

cases.source: Ada knows that the document is authentic. Therefore the document is authentic.
cases.reason: Factivity needs epistemic semantics or an explicit extra axiom.

cases.source: This outcome is possible. Therefore this outcome is necessary.
cases.reason: Possibility and necessity must not be flattened into the same proposition.

cases.source: Usually honest witnesses speak truthfully. Rowan is an honest witness. Therefore Rowan speaks truthfully.
cases.reason: Usually is defeasible, not a universal quantifier.

cases.source: Every reader admired a book. Therefore there is one book that every reader admired.
cases.reason: The first sentence has distributive versus shared-witness scope ambiguity; the source does not settle it.

cases.source: What makes a belief justified? Is certainty required?
The lecture began at noon. Its topic was personal identity. The room had twelve chairs.
cases.reason: A description, not a premise-conclusion argument.
